findings.detail: 1 evidence classification violation(s) downgraded by registry

D1 [verdict; criteriaAssessments C1 (assessment, strengths), C3; CL18, CL19; alternatives 'Option (a) with noise tuning' and 'Recommended hybrid'; counterargument[0]; K31, K32, K36] The new out-of-hours comparison counts secondary standby hours the same as primary hours for option (a), and then sets that against follow-the-sun with no secondary. K31 (2*(168-40)/9 = 28.44 h), K32 (12.44 local-night h) and K36 (10.67 weekend h) all double the primary figure because a secondary is added. A secondary is only paged on escalation, so it carries far less interruption load than a primary. The draft itself says how often the secondary would be paged is unknown (E12 limitations). The draft's own rollout also allows a daytime secondary within follow-the-sun, so the comparison does not hold like for like. Even so, the 28.4 h vs 9.8-11 h gap is used as a main argument: the verdict, C1 strengths, alternatives ('less than half the out-of-hours load per person'), and the first counterargument response. The fairer like-for-like figure is the primary-only 14.2 h (K30) vs 9.8-11 h. That gap is still real but much smaller (about 23-31% lower). The ranking probably survives on the zero-local-night point, but the size of the out-of-hours advantage is overstated.

D2 [verdict; criteriaAssessments C4 assessment; counterargument[3]] The verdict and C4 say 'Weekend and holiday call-outs fall under the s.9 ban' and 'Weekend and holiday call-outs are Sunday or holiday work'. ArbZG s.9 covers Sundays and public holidays only. Saturday is a Werktag, so it falls under s.3, as E23 itself notes ('Werktage, Mon-Sat'). CL20 gets this right ('Sunday and holiday'), so the draft contradicts itself. The packet's E20 applicability text has the same slip, but the draft should not have repeated it.

D3 [criteriaAssessments C3 weaknesses; CL21; edgeCasesAndFailureModes (Sunday item)] The s.11 rule of at least 15 work-free Sundays a year is listed as a constraint that 'would cut Berlin's capacity further' (C3 weaknesses) and is something counsel must confirm. The draft's own figure is about 13 on-call weekends a year per Berlin engineer, which leaves about 39 Sundays a year off call. So the 15-Sunday floor cannot bind under the proposed rotation. Only the substitute-rest-day rule (within 2 weeks after a Sunday call-out) is a real capacity factor. The draft does not make this simple check and overstates the s.11 risk.

openDecisiveGaps: What is the hour-of-day and weekday/weekend distribution of actionable pages after the three noise alerts are removed (raw timestamped logs)? How would it split between the Berlin 22:00-10:00 PT half and the SF half?

How often would a secondary actually be paged under option (a), and would a same-office daytime secondary within follow-the-sun close the reliability gap? This sets the true burden and benefit of the secondary role in the (a) vs (b) comparison.
Can each office independently handle every paging alert type (runbooks, access, service ownership)?
Does labour counsel confirm that Sunday and holiday incident call-outs fall under ArbZG s.10(1) no.14? Does a collective agreement with s.7/s.12 opening clauses cover the Berlin entity?
